assessments.reasoning: The title page identifies Colmerauer and Roussel's November 1992 manuscript. A fresh HTTP 200 response matched the registered complete PDF digest. Inspected the exact passage on physical page 6. The authors describe a predicate N(x,y) for each nonterminal. It holds when that nonterminal derives the prefix of x before remainder y. They describe lists for the two arguments and a clause encoding that avoids explicit list concatenation. The claim describes the early analyzer’s grammar encoding in the Marseille project. The manual syntax of later grammar-rule notations and their implementation details are outside scope. The paragraph places the binary pair in the grammar representation. It separately allows additional parameters to propagate or compute information. It does not impose a two-argument limit on every predicate the analyzer uses.
